original_value: Recent developments in machine learning engendered many algorithms designed to solve diverse problems. More complicated tasks can be solved since numerous features included in much larger datasets are extracted by deep learning architectures. The prevailing transfer learning method in recent years enables researchers and engineers to conduct experiments within limited computing and time constraints. In this paper, we evaluated traditional machine learning, deep learning and transfer learning methodologies to compare their characteristics by training and testing on a butterfly dataset, and determined the optimal model to deploy in an Android application. The application can detect the category of a butterfly by either capturing a real-time picture of a butterfly or choosing one picture from the mobile gallery.

result.paraphrase: Recent advances in machine learning have produced many algorithms for solving a wide range of problems. Deep learning architectures can address more complex tasks by extracting numerous features from much larger datasets. In recent years, transfer learning has become the dominant method, allowing researchers and engineers to run experiments under limited computing and time resources. In this paper, we compared traditional machine learning, deep learning, and transfer learning approaches by training and testing them on a butterfly dataset, then selected the best model for deployment in an Android app. The app identifies a butterfly’s class either by taking a real-time photo of it or by selecting an image from the mobile gallery.
